recorded: Original served by webpack-dev-server 5.2.2 with webpack 5.101.0 and PixiJS 8.11.0, and driven in headless Google Chrome 152. It ran with npx webpack-dev-server --port $PORT --no-open instead of npm start, which fixes port 8080 and opens a browser, and no file was patched. The worker loads TensorFlow.js from jsdelivr without using it, so the page needs network access. The game draws on a canvas, so a script that runs before the page's own catches the PixiJS application through its devtools hook (__PIXI_APP_INIT__), records each text the stage shows in session storage, which survives the reload of a replay, and keeps what the page logs. Every prediction is the same point, and every case passed in each of 22 runs, most of them with the parts' cases running at the same time.

cases.name: predicts the same point every 200 ms and shows it in the HUD

page.init: (() => { if (window !== window.top) return; globalThis.__PIXI_APP_INIT__ = (app) => { globalThis.pixiApp = app; }; globalThis.loggedMessages = []; const log = console.log.bind(console); console.log = (...parts) => { loggedMessages.push({ text: parts.join(' '), time: performance.now() }); log(...parts); }; globalThis.canvasTexts = () => { const texts = []; const visit = (node) => { if (!node.visible) return; if (typeof node.text === 'string' && node.text !== '') texts.push(node.text); node.children.forEach(visit); }; if (globalThis.pixiApp) visit(pixiApp.stage); return texts; }; sessionStorage.setItem('pageLoads', String(Number(sessionStorage.getItem('pageLoads')) + 1)); const shownTexts = JSON.parse(sessionStorage.getItem('shownTexts') ?? '[]'); const record = () => { const fresh = canvasTexts().filter((text) => !shownTexts.includes(text)); if (fresh.length === 0) return; shownTexts.push(...fresh); sessionStorage.setItem('shownTexts', JSON.stringify(shownTexts)); }; setInterval(record, 50); addEventListener('pagehide', record); })()

steps.read: (() => { const times = loggedMessages.filter(({ text }) => text.startsWith('🎯 ')).map(({ time }) => time); const intervals = times.slice(1).map((time, index) => time - times[index]).sort((left, right) => left - right); const median = intervals[Math.floor(intervals.length / 2)]; return median >= 150 && median <= 300; })()
